content:
nina: quick heads-up — during a customer onprem deploy review we found a kubelet-access path from the edge-agent pod when hostNetwork: true is used. can we treat this as P1 for private deploy hardening? :eyes:
sam: ok can you paste the logs/trace? which port/endpoint?
nina: reproduced locally. edge-agent can reach 127.0.0.1:10250 and GET /pods which returns podSpec including mounted secret refs. short dump attached below:```GET /api/v1/namespaces/default/pods?fieldSelector=metadata.name%3Dedge-agent 200 OK
{"items": [{"metadata": {"name": "edge-agent"}, "spec": {"containers": [...], "hostNetwork": true}}]}```
omar: if that's true it allows reading pod specs, not secrets directly, but combined with mounted volumes could leak. immediate mitigation: block egress from edge-agent to node localhost:10250 via NetworkPolicy or iptables. i'll push a quick rule for canary clusters.
sec-bot: [alert] CVE-style indicator: KUBELET_LOCAL_ACCESS_EXPOSURE detected on private deploy template v0.9.3
jia: from KMS perspective, we should check decrypt logs. if attacker can read pod specs they might find KMS key references (keystore URIs) or service account tokens. we need to confirm whether any decrypt calls correlate with suspicious SA. can security team provide candidate svcaccounts?
irene: timeline: treat as potential data-exfil vector. notify legal if customer data could be affected. also we need an incident log: initial detection, repro steps, mitigation, affected clusters, customer notification plan.
sam: immediate actions I suggest: 1) revoke any ClusterRoleBindings created by old edge-agent versions (run `kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o wide | grep edge-agent` and delete suspicious ones), 2) create a NetworkPolicy that denies pod->hostNetwork:10250 egress for edge-agent namespace, 3) rotate service-account tokens for tenants flagged, 4) check KMS audit logs for decrypts. I'll take 1+2.
nina: sample NetworkPolicy to apply quickly:```apiVersion: networking.k8s.io/v1
kind: NetworkPolicy
metadata:
  name: deny-edge-agent-kubelet
  namespace: edge-tenant
spec:
  podSelector:
    matchLabels:
      app: edge-agent
  policyTypes:
  - Egress
  egress:
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 127.0.0.1/32
      ports:
      - protocol: TCP
        port: 10250
  - to:
    - ipBlock:
        cidr: 0.0.0.0/0
    # allow other egress per existing rules
```
omar: note: NetworkPolicy won't block hostNetwork traffic on some CNI implementations if the pod is hostNetwork itself. if edge-agent runs hostNetwork:true, we need to change the deployment to not use hostNetwork or run a host-level firewall (iptables) as fallback. prioritizing patch of agent image to remove hostNetwork by default.
jia: on KMS side: query CloudKMS/Audit logs for entries with principalName containing "edge-agent" or the suspected service account. also check for decrypt operations in the window 2024-03-01T00:00:00Z..2024-03-02T00:00:00Z (example). if we find any, capture the ciphertext ID and rotation state.
irene: assign roles: sam owns patch rollout + netpol for canary clusters, jia owns KMS audit and rotation plan, omar owns hostNetwork removal plan + host firewall fallback, nina owns repro write-up and detection signature for sec-bot. set a 4hr SLA for mitigation on canaries, 24hr for full fleet.
sam: quick commands I'll run now:```# list edge cluster CRBs
kubectl get clusterrolebinding -o json | jq '.items[] | select(.subjects[]?.name | test("edge-agent")) | .metadata.name'
# apply canary netpol
kubectl apply -f deny-edge-agent-kubelet.yaml -n edge-tenant```
nina: detection rules to add to cluster-agent: blocklisted egress to 127.0.0.1:10250 from pods labeled app=edge-agent, alert to #eng-security. adding a short Snort-like signature to sec-bot.
sec-bot: action logged: detection rule added by nina at 2024-03-01T14:18:00Z.
omar: longer-term: do not run edge-agent with hostNetwork. update installer (ansible/helm) to reject hostNetwork=true unless explicitly approved with justification. add a preflight check in the private-deploy CLI.
jia: KMS followup: if decrypts found, rotate the affected key and add envelope key rotation for tenants using edge-agent. I'll prepare rotation playbook and test on staging.
irene: communication: do not notify customers until we confirm decrypts. prepare holding statement and timeline. legal on standby.
sam: i'll push the canary netpol now and follow up with a short post in #eng-security with affected cluster list. tagging @jia @omar @nina for updates. :thumbsup:
nina: thanks — will paste repro steps + minimal PoC in thread after I scrub customer identifiers.
omar: creating a remediation ticket and adding to oncall runbook: PRIV-EDGE-K8S-10250.
jia: noted, starting KMS audit queries now.
irene: good work team. keep updates here. we will reconvene in 2 hours for status. :lock:
